prompt.context: PaintCo is a major European industrial goods company that focuses mainly on coatings. Its performance coatings division wants to develop a growth strategy while maintaining high margins by assessing the potential of its different businesses. One business under review is Vehicle Refinishing — repairing scratches and other paint damage on cars — where PaintCo is currently ranked #4 globally. Vehicle Refinishing is one of the more profitable businesses in PaintCo's portfolio, selling both premium and commodity refinishing products alongside a wide array of services including training and free equipment.
prompt.question: The client wants to find out what EBITDA growth it can expect from its Vehicle Refinishing business going forward. How would you approach this?

clarifying_info.q: What geographies does PaintCo operate in?
clarifying_info.a: PaintCo is a major European company but competes globally in Vehicle Refinishing.

clarifying_info.q: Are there specific growth targets or time horizons?
clarifying_info.a: No specific target has been given; a directional assessment is sufficient.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current product mix?
clarifying_info.a: Half of products are premium paints selling at 25 EUR/liter; the other half are commodity paints selling at 15 EUR/liter. This mix is not expected to change.

exhibits.title: Cost Bar Slide (Figure 1)
exhibits.shows: A cost breakdown bar chart comparing cost elements (raw materials, sales/SG&A, production, R&D, overhead) for premium vs. commodity products and a benchmark, showing relative sizes of each cost component as EUR per liter.
exhibits.data: Raw materials and sales/SG&A are the largest cost elements. Raw material cost is in line with benchmark. Sales/SG&A cost for commodity: ~4 EUR/liter. Total cost for commodity before savings: ~13 EUR/liter. Total cost for premium: ~19 EUR/liter.

exhibits.title: Customer Survey Slide (Figure 2)
exhibits.shows: A customer survey showing the relative importance of service vs. price for premium and commodity customers.
exhibits.data: Premium customers give high importance to service. Commodity customers consider price as the key factor.

framework: EBITDA growth can be split into three main drivers: (1) Market growth, (2) Acquisitions, (3) Profitability increase
Market growth: analyze bottom-up drivers of volume and price in the refinishing market
Acquisitions: screen potential targets and assess synergies and margin impact
Profitability increase: assess pricing power and cost reduction opportunities across raw materials, production, SG&A, R&D, and overhead
Alternative revenue-tree structure: Revenue increase (price/unit, mix effects, volume via acquisition or market growth) minus Cost decrease

questions.prompt: Step 2: Estimate the growth of the refinishing market bottom-up. Walk through the key drivers.
questions.guidance: Candidate should creatively decompose market size into volume and price drivers. A strong answer works through: number of cars (driven by population growth + cars/person, both positive, especially in emerging markets), car accidents involving paint damage (slightly negative due to better roads and safety tech), distance travelled per car (roughly flat), accidents per km (declining due to infrastructure and safety equipment), % of damage actually repainted (roughly flat — insurance coverage up, but more cars declared total loss, non-insured repair rate flat), paint per car (declining due to thinner layers), and paint price (strongly positive). Net result: modest positive market growth overall, with price as a key upward driver.

math.setup: No precise calculation required; directional signs for each driver are sufficient.
steps: Number of cars: positive (population growth + more cars per person, especially ++)
Car accidents involving paint damage: negative (better safety, better roads)
Accidents per km: negative (road infrastructure + safety equipment)
% damage repainted: flat (insurance coverage up +, but % total loss also up -, non-insured repair flat)
Paint per car: negative (fewer layers, thinner layers)
math.answer: Market growth is net positive, driven primarily by rising paint prices and increasing car ownership; partially offset by fewer accidents and less paint per repair.

questions.prompt: Step 3: Assess potential acquisitions in Vehicle Refinishing.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize the strategic complexity: larger targets in Vehicle Refinishing often have high synergies with Automotive OEM (factory) paints, which PaintCo does not sell. OEM paints carry much lower margins. Therefore, acquiring these targets means either paying for synergies PaintCo cannot realize, or acquiring a lower-margin business that undermines PaintCo's profitability objective. Conclusion: acquisitions in this segment will be difficult to execute attractively.

questions.prompt: Step 4a: Looking at Exhibit 1 (cost bar), what do you observe about the cost structure, especially comparing premium vs. commodity products?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that raw materials and sales/SG&A are the largest cost elements. Raw material cost is in line with benchmark (no easy savings there). However, sales/SG&A costs are not in line with benchmark and are notably high — and critically, SG&A is almost as high in commodity as in premium products, despite commodity customers not valuing service. This represents an inefficiency: PaintCo is spending similar service dollars on commodity customers who only care about price.

questions.prompt: Step 4b: After seeing Exhibit 2 (customer survey), what cost action would you recommend, and what would the new EBITDA margin be if SG&A for commodity products were cut by 50%?
questions.guidance: Exhibit 2 confirms that premium customers value service highly, while commodity customers are price-driven. This supports cutting SG&A services for commodity customers without meaningful revenue loss. Candidate should then calculate the new blended EBITDA margin.

math.setup: Current commodity SG&A: 4 EUR/liter. Cut by 50% = save 2 EUR/liter. New commodity total cost: original ~13 EUR/liter minus 2 = 11 EUR/liter. Premium total cost remains 19 EUR/liter. Mix is 50/50. Average price = 50% x 15 + 50% x 25 = 20 EUR/liter. Average cost = 50% x 11 + 50% x 19 = 15 EUR/liter.
steps: Commodity SG&A savings: 4 EUR/liter x 50% = 2 EUR/liter

questions.prompt: Step 5: Given everything you know, how would you position the Vehicle Refinishing business in PaintCo's portfolio? Invest, divest, or maintain?
questions.guidance: Candidate should synthesize all findings into a clear recommendation. Strong answers cover: (1) good market growth and margin profile — one of the more profitable businesses in the portfolio; (2) profitability improvement opportunity via SG&A rationalization on commodity; (3) #4 global position leaves room to grow market share; (4) acquisitions will be difficult due to OEM paint entanglement and margin dilution. Conclusion: invest if possible (organic growth + margin improvement), maintain otherwise. Divesting would be value-destructive given the attractive profitability.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the drivers of market growth in the Vehicle Refinishing market? Walk through each lever and indicate whether it is a positive, negative, or neutral factor.

categories.name: Volume — Number of Cars
ideas: Cars per person (especially in emerging markets): strongly positive

categories.name: Volume — Accident Rate
ideas: Car accidents involving paint damage: negative overall
Distance travelled per car: roughly flat
Accidents per km: negative (better road infrastructure, improved safety equipment in cars)

categories.name: Volume — Repair Rate
ideas: % of damage actually repainted: roughly flat
Insurance coverage: positive (more insured cars get repaired)
% insured cars declared total loss: negative (reduces actual repair work)

categories.name: Volume — Paint per Repair
ideas: Thickness of each layer: negative (technology improvements reduce paint used)

categories.name: Price
ideas: Price of paint per liter: strongly positive (premium formulations, inflation)

recommendation: Invest in Vehicle Refinishing if capacity allows — the business offers good growth prospects and is among the most profitable in PaintCo's portfolio
If full investment is not feasible, maintain the current position and focus on organic margin improvement through SG&A rationalization on commodity products
risks: #4 global position means limited pricing power relative to top-3 competitors
Acquisitions are structurally difficult due to OEM paint entanglement and associated margin dilution
Commodity segment profitability depends on successfully executing SG&A cuts without customer churn
next_steps: Implement 50% SG&A cut on commodity products and monitor customer retention
Explore organic growth opportunities to improve global ranking above #4
Re-evaluate acquisition landscape periodically as market consolidates
